title: Token Waterfall Attribution Ledger and KV-influence Diagnostics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a deterministic way to reconcile per-request billing and latency SLOs with low-level runtime behaviour. Current metrics aggregate at request or route level and miss how KV cache hits/misses, micro-kernel scheduling and batching interact to create token-level variance. This ticket implements a Token Waterfall Attribution Ledger (TWAL) and accompanying KV-influence diagnostics to make per-token latency, KV impact, and inferred cost attributable and queryable in dashboards and billing reconciliation pipelines.

Goals:
- Emit enriched per-token spans and lightweight ledger entries that capture stage-by-stage timings (cache lookup, kernel exec, GPU transfer, attention, beam/decoding) and KV cache hit metadata.
- Provide a small, efficient ledger format that can be attached to sampled traces and also emitted as a compact metric/log for high-volume aggregation.
- Surface new Grafana dashboards and alerting that show token-level waterfalls, kv-hit contribution to latency, and token-cost delta estimate.
- Allow rollbacks/fallback to coarse attribution when TWAL is disabled to avoid regressions in latency.

Design summary (high level):
- Instrumentation: enrich request traces with per-token lightweight ledger entries. Each token ledger record includes: token_index, token_text_hash, model_variant, stage, duration_ms, kv_hit (true/false), kv_latency_ms, batch_id, kernel_ms, device (GPU/CPU), quant_mode, and correlating request_id.
- Sampling: default 1% request-level sampling, stratified by model_variant and latency percentiles. A separate high-frequency kv-only sample emits only kv-hit counters for aggregation (to answer long-tail KV impact without full token ledgers).
- Wire format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) ledger entries with a compact schema and an encoded token_text_hash to avoid raw PII / prompt leakage. Example telemetry metric prefix: rw.token.ledger and trace span name: rw.span.token.ledger.
- Pathing: ledger entries are attached as child spans when sampling tracing; for high-volume metric flows they are published to the metrics/log pipeline via a dedicated router (agent -> OTLP -> Collector -> Kafka -> consumer jobs).

Telemetry fields (canonical names):
- rw.token.ledger.record: {request_id, token_idx, token_hash, model, variant, stage, duration_ms, kv_hit, kv_latency_ms, kernel_ms, device, batch_size, quant_profile, timestamp}
- rw.token.kv.counter: label kv_hit=true/false, model, variant, shard
- rw.token.latency.histogram: token_latency_ms (buckets), labels: model, variant, stage

Implementation approach and milestones:
1) Proto-impl (backend runtime): add micro-timing probes in the serving runtime at stage boundaries (cache lookup start/end, prefill, kernel launch, kernel complete, emit finalize). Expose a ring-buffer ledger in-memory per-request when sampling enabled. (Owner: Runtime infra)
2) Lite export path (low-overhead): implement a binary-compact encoder + ndjson fallback for debug. Route ledger entries through the existing OTLP agent; add Kafka topic token-ledgers for downstream consumers. (Owner: Telemetry)
3) Tracing integration: map ledger entries to OpenTelemetry spans for Jaeger/Zipkin. Span enrichment should be optional flag controlled by route-level config. (Owner: Tracing)
4) Aggregation jobs: consumer job that converts ledgers to aggregated metrics (kv-hit ratios, per-stage P50/P95/P99, delta cost estimates). Output to Cortex/Prometheus for dashboards. (Owner: Observability)
5) Dashboards & Alerts: new Grafana panels: Token Waterfall Explorer, KV Latency Contribution, Token Cost Hotspots, and Token Path SLO deviation. Include runbook for when token SLOs spike. (Owner: DX/Monitoring)

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumented runtime emits ledger entries for sampled requests with <2% p95 overhead on a benchmark workload.
- Aggregation job produces rw.token.* metrics with matching labels and documented schema.
- Grafana dashboards display token-level waterfall for a sample request and aggregated kv contribution charts.
- End-to-end test harness can replay saved ledgers and validate aggregation correctness against golden output.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests around encoder/decoder for ledger entries.
- Host-level microbenchmarks to measure throughput/latency overhead (setup: sequence length 512, batch sizes 1..8).
- Synthetic workload that forces KV cache hit/miss patterns to validate attribution.
- Integration test: enable tracing + ledger sampling in staging; verify ledgers reach Kafka consumer and aggregate metrics within 60s.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature gate behind route/tenant toggle.
- Canary: 1% of traffic for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> 50% -> global. Monitor error budget and p95 serve latency.
- Fallback: if ledger path causes regressions, automatically disable ledger export and keep only coarse counters.

Dependencies:
- Telemetry pipeline (Kafka OTLP consumer) readiness and topic allocation.
- Observability: user-permissions for Grafana provisioning.
- Runtime kernel hooks for precise micro-timing.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Full token text vs hashed token: using token_text_hash protects prompts but prevents human-readable debugging. We will include sample-request text in a separate, strictly-controlled debug export.
- Sampling rate: higher sampling increases fidelity but adds cost; we plan stratified adaptive sampling keyed by model_variant and latency percentile.
- Storage/ingest cost: token ledgers are high-volume; prefer compact encoding + downstream aggregation rather than raw storage retention.
